prayer.fard.fajr.title: Fajr
prayer.fard.fajr.subtitle: Dawn Prayer
prayer.fard.fajr.rakat: Fard: 2 Rakat · 2 Sunnah before is standard
prayer.fard.fajr.time: Start: True dawn  ·  End: Before sunrise
prayer.fard.fajr.note: Fajr starts when true dawn light appears and ends at sunrise. Check your local prayer timetable.
prayer.fard.fajr.virtue: Glad tidings of Paradise are reported for strictly observing Fajr and Asr.
prayer.fard.dhuhr.title: Dhuhr
prayer.fard.dhuhr.subtitle: Noon Prayer
prayer.fard.dhuhr.rakat: Fard: 4 Rakat · Sunnah distribution varies by school
prayer.fard.dhuhr.time: Start: After sun passes zenith  ·  End: Start of Asr
prayer.fard.dhuhr.note: Dhuhr begins when the sun passes the meridian. The start of Asr depends on calculation method.
prayer.fard.dhuhr.virtue: Praying on time is among the most beloved deeds to Allah.
prayer.fard.asr.title: Asr
prayer.fard.asr.subtitle: Afternoon Prayer
prayer.fard.asr.time: Start: Asr enters  ·  End: Before sunset
prayer.fard.asr.note: The start time of Asr differs by school (Shafi/Hanafi). Follow your local mosque time.
prayer.fard.asr.virtue: Glad tidings of Paradise are reported for strictly observing Fajr and Asr.
prayer.fard.maghrib.title: Maghrib
prayer.fard.maghrib.subtitle: Sunset Prayer
prayer.fard.maghrib.rakat: Fard: 3 Rakat · 2 Sunnah after is standard
prayer.fard.maghrib.time: Start: Right after sunset  ·  End: Before twilight fades
prayer.fard.maghrib.note: Maghrib begins immediately after complete sunset. Its window is short, so pray promptly.
prayer.fard.maghrib.virtue: The five daily prayers expiate sins committed between them, provided major sins are avoided.
prayer.fard.isha.title: Isha
prayer.fard.isha.subtitle: Night Prayer
prayer.fard.isha.rakat: Fard: 4 Rakat · Followed by Sunnah and Witr
prayer.fard.isha.time: Start: Evening twilight disappears  ·  Preferably before midnight
prayer.fard.isha.note: Isha starts after evening red twilight disappears. Midnight means the middle of the night between sunset and dawn.
prayer.fard.isha.virtue: Special virtue is described for attending Isha and Fajr prayers in congregation.
prayer.other.sunnah.title: Sunnah Prayers
prayer.other.sunnah.subtitle: Before & After Fard
prayer.other.sunnah.rakat: Example: 2 before Fajr; 2 before/after other Fard
prayer.other.sunnah.time: Before or after associated obligatory prayer
prayer.other.sunnah.note: The count of emphasized and non-emphasized Sunnah varies across schools. Follow your family/teacher.
prayer.other.sunnah.virtue: Glad tidings of a house in Paradise are reported for offering 12 regular Sunnah rakat daily.
prayer.other.witr.title: Witr
prayer.other.witr.subtitle: Odd Rakat after Isha
prayer.other.witr.rakat: Odd rakat; 1 or 3 rakat methods vary by school
prayer.other.witr.note: Method and rakat count for Witr have minor differences across schools. Practice as taught.
prayer.other.witr.rule: Pray odd rakat after Isha; learn Qunut and posture rules from your teacher.
prayer.other.witr.virtue: Witr is an odd-numbered prayer; the Prophet ﷺ strongly encouraged offering it.
prayer.other.tahajjud.title: Tahajjud
prayer.other.tahajjud.subtitle: Night Voluntary Prayer
prayer.other.tahajjud.rakat: Prayed in sets of 2; no fixed maximum
prayer.other.tahajjud.time: After waking from sleep following Isha, before Fajr
prayer.other.tahajjud.note: Best prayed in the last third of the night. Keep it gentle when tired.
prayer.other.tahajjud.rule: Generally prayed in 2 rakat sets. Finish the night prayer with Witr.
prayer.other.tahajjud.virtue: The night prayer is described as the best voluntary prayer after the obligatory prayers.
prayer.other.ishraq.title: Ishraq
prayer.other.ishraq.subtitle: Post-Sunrise Voluntary
prayer.other.ishraq.time: After sunrise prohibited time passes; before Dhuhr
prayer.other.ishraq.note: Do not pray immediately as the sun rises. Wait 15-20 minutes after local sunrise.
prayer.other.ishraq.rule: Offer 2 rakat like standard voluntary prayers, avoiding prohibited rising sun times.
prayer.other.ishraq.virtue: An opportunity to begin the morning with remembrance of Allah and voluntary prayer.
prayer.other.duha.title: Duha / Chasht
prayer.other.duha.subtitle: Mid-Morning Prayer
prayer.other.duha.rakat: Minimum 2 Rakat; multiple sets can be prayed
prayer.other.duha.time: From late morning until before Dhuhr
prayer.other.duha.note: Ishraq is often considered the early part of Duha prayer.
prayer.other.duha.rule: Pray in 2 rakat sets according to your capacity and custom.
prayer.other.duha.virtue: Duha is a well-known voluntary worship; can be performed regularly as able.
prayer.other.tarawih.title: Tarawih
prayer.other.tarawih.subtitle: Ramadan Night Prayer
prayer.other.tarawih.rakat: Rakat counts vary across recognized traditions (8/20)
prayer.other.tarawih.note: Tarawih can be offered in congregation or individually. Follow your local mosque.
prayer.other.tarawih.rule: Offered in 2 rakat intervals after Isha during Ramadan.
prayer.other.tarawih.virtue: Standing in night prayer during Ramadan with faith and seeking reward has great virtue.
prayer.other.jumah.title: Jumah Prayer
prayer.other.jumah.subtitle: Friday Congregation
prayer.other.jumah.rakat: 2 Fard rakat in congregation following Khutbah
prayer.other.jumah.note: Learn the obligations and conditions of Friday prayer from a knowledgeable elder/scholar.
prayer.other.jumah.rule: Listen attentively to the Khutbah, then pray 2 Fard rakat with the Imam.
prayer.other.jumah.virtue: The prayers from one Friday to the next expiate minor sins, if major sins are avoided.
prayer.other.eid.title: Eid Prayer
prayer.other.eid.subtitle: Eid al-Fitr & Eid al-Adha
prayer.other.eid.rakat: 2 Rakat; additional Takbirs vary by school
prayer.other.eid.time: On Eid morning, after the sun rises well
prayer.other.eid.note: Follow the Imam in the number and sequence of extra Takbirs.
prayer.other.eid.rule: Prayed in 2 rakat congregation with extra Takbirs; step-by-step with the Imam.
prayer.other.eid.virtue: Eid prayer in congregation is an act of gratitude and joy for Muslims.
prayer.other.janazah.title: Janazah Prayer
prayer.other.janazah.subtitle: Supplication for Deceased Muslim
prayer.other.janazah.time: When the funeral is prepared, in congregation
prayer.other.janazah.note: Offered entirely while standing. Learn the supplications with elders/scholars.
prayer.other.janazah.rule: Stand for 4 Takbirs with no Ruku or Sujud; recite supplications as taught.
prayer.other.janazah.virtue: Tremendous reward (Qirat) is described in Hadith for joining the funeral prayer.
duas.habit_desc: Learn one dua and discover its meaning.
duas.disclaimer: Arabic text and Hadith numbers are cross-referenced with Sunnah.com.
duas.item.wake.title: Waking Up
duas.item.wake.meaning: All praise is for Allah who gave us life after causing us to die, and unto Him is the resurrection.
duas.item.morning_protection.title: Morning Protection
duas.item.morning_protection.meaning: In the name of Allah, with whose name nothing can cause harm in the earth nor in the heavens, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
duas.item.evening_adhkar.title: Evening Dua
duas.item.evening_adhkar.meaning: O Allah, by You we enter the morning and by You we enter the evening, by You we live and by You we die, and to You is the resurrection.
duas.item.morning_sabah.title: Morning Praise & Gratitude
duas.item.morning_sabah.meaning: We have reached the morning and all dominion belongs to Allah, all praise is for Allah. There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah alone, without partner.
duas.item.food.title: Before Eating
duas.item.food_after.title: After Eating
duas.item.food_after.meaning: All praise is due to Allah who has given us food and drink, satisfied us and sheltered us.
duas.item.wudu_after.title: After Wudu
duas.item.wudu_after.meaning: I bear witness that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah alone, without partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and messenger.
duas.item.clothes.title: Wearing New Clothes
duas.item.clothes.meaning: Praise be to Allah who has clothed me with this garment and provided it for me without any power or strength on my part.
duas.item.restroom.title: Entering the Restroom
duas.item.restroom.meaning: In the name of Allah. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from impure male and female jinns.
duas.item.restroom_exit.title: Leaving the Restroom
duas.item.restroom_exit.meaning: I seek Your forgiveness, O Allah.
duas.item.leave_home.title: Leaving the House
duas.item.leave_home.meaning: In the name of Allah, I trust in Allah; there is no power and no strength except with Allah.
duas.item.enter_home.title: Entering the House
duas.item.enter_home.meaning: In the name of Allah we enter, and in the name of Allah we leave, and upon our Lord we rely.
duas.item.mosque_enter.title: Entering the Mosque
duas.item.mosque_enter.meaning: I seek refuge in Allah the Supreme and in His Noble Face from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah. O Allah, open for me the doors of Your mercy.
duas.item.mosque_exit.title: Leaving the Mosque
duas.item.mosque_exit.meaning: In the name of Allah, peace and blessings be upon the Messenger of Allah. O Allah, I ask You from Your bounty. O Allah, protect me from the accursed Satan.
duas.item.sleep.title: Before Going to Sleep
duas.item.sleep.meaning: In Your name, O Allah, I die and I live.
duas.item.sleep_ayatul_kursi.title: Ayatul Kursi Before Sleep
duas.item.sleep_ayatul_kursi.meaning: Allah! There is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all existence. Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep.
duas.item.nightmare.title: Nightmare or Fear in Sleep
duas.item.nightmare.meaning: I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from His wrath and punishment, from the evil of His slaves, and from the whisperings of devils and their presence.
duas.item.travel.title: Setting Out on Travel
duas.item.travel.meaning: In the name of Allah, praise be to Allah. Glory is to Him Who has subjected this to us, and we could never have it by our efforts. And to our Lord we shall return.
duas.item.travel_return.title: Returning from Travel
duas.item.travel_return.meaning: Allah is the Greatest (3x). Glory to Him Who subjected this to us. We return, repenting, worshipping, and praising our Lord.
duas.item.rain.title: During Rain
duas.item.rain.meaning: O Allah, make it a beneficial and blessed rain.
duas.item.sneeze.title: When Sneezing
duas.item.sneeze_response.title: Replying to a Sneezing Person
duas.item.sneeze_response.meaning: May Allah have mercy upon you.
duas.item.anxiety.title: During Distress or Anxiety
duas.item.anxiety.meaning: Allah is sufficient for me; there is no deity except Him. Upon Him I have relied, and He is the Lord of the Great Throne.
duas.item.forgiveness.title: Sayyid al-Istighfar
duas.item.forgiveness.meaning: O Allah, You are my Lord; there is no deity except You. You created me and I am Your servant, and I abide by Your covenant as best as I can.
duas.item.parents.title: Dua for Parents
duas.item.parents.meaning: My Lord, have mercy upon them as they brought me up when I was small.

qaida.letter.alif.makhraj: Empty space in the mouth and throat (Jawf) with outgoing breath.
qaida.letter.ba.makhraj: Produced by bringing both lips together firmly on the wet part.
qaida.letter.ta.makhraj: Tip of the tongue touching the roots of the upper front teeth.
qaida.letter.tha.makhraj: Tip of the tongue gently touching the edges of the upper front teeth.
qaida.letter.jeem.makhraj: Middle of the tongue touching the hard palate above it.
qaida.letter.ha.makhraj: Middle of the throat with a clear, smooth, breathy sound.
qaida.letter.kha.makhraj: Upper throat closest to the mouth with a full, raspy tone.
qaida.letter.dal.makhraj: Tip of the tongue touching the base of the upper front teeth.
qaida.letter.dhal.makhraj: Tip of the tongue against the tips of the upper front teeth with soft sound.
qaida.letter.ra.makhraj: Tip of the tongue touching the upper gums near the front teeth.
qaida.letter.zay.makhraj: Tip of the tongue close to the lower front teeth with a buzzing whistle.
qaida.letter.seen.makhraj: Tip of the tongue near the lower front teeth with a whistling hiss.
qaida.letter.sheen.makhraj: Middle of the tongue raised towards the roof of the palate.
qaida.letter.sad.makhraj: Tip of the tongue at lower teeth, tongue raised and thickened (heavy).
qaida.letter.dad.makhraj: One or both sides of the tongue touching the upper molar teeth.
qaida.letter.toa.makhraj: Tip of the tongue at the roots of upper front teeth with deep, heavy tone.
qaida.letter.zoa.makhraj: Tip of the tongue against the tips of upper front teeth with heavy tone.
qaida.letter.ayn.makhraj: Middle of the throat squeezed smoothly without straining.
qaida.letter.ghayn.makhraj: Upper throat closest to the mouth with a smooth, gargling sound.
qaida.letter.fa.makhraj: Edges of the upper front teeth touching the wet inside of the lower lip.
qaida.letter.qaf.makhraj: Deep back of the tongue raised against the soft palate.
qaida.letter.kaf.makhraj: Back of the tongue touching the hard palate slightly in front of Qaf.
qaida.letter.lam.makhraj: Tip and sides of the tongue touching the upper gums.
qaida.letter.meem.makhraj: Produced by closing both lips together with light nasal resonance.
qaida.letter.noon.makhraj: Tip of the tongue against the upper gums with nasal resonance.
qaida.letter.ha_soft.makhraj: Bottom of the throat (chest level) with a gentle outgoing breath.
qaida.letter.waw.makhraj: Rounding both lips forward without closing them completely.
qaida.letter.ya.makhraj: Middle of the tongue raised towards the upper palate.
qaida.step.1.title: Mufradat
qaida.step.1.desc: Single Arabic letters recognition and pure articulation points.
qaida.step.2.title: Murakkabat
qaida.step.2.desc: Letter forms in initial, medial, final and connected script.
qaida.step.3.title: Harakat
qaida.step.3.desc: Short vowel marks: Fatha (a), Kasra (i), and Damma (u).
qaida.step.4.title: Tanween
qaida.step.5.title: Khari Harakat
qaida.step.5.desc: Standing Fatha, Inverted Damma, and Standing Kasra prolonged for 1 Alif.
qaida.step.6.title: Hurufe Layyin
qaida.step.6.desc: Soft letters Waw and Yaa preceded by Fatha pronounced smoothly.
qaida.step.7.title: Sukoon & Jazm
qaida.step.7.desc: Silent resting sign connecting letters in joined syllables.
qaida.step.8.title: Shaddah
qaida.step.8.desc: Doubling mark giving emphasis and double duration to letters.
qaida.step.9.title: Noon Sakin & Tanween
qaida.step.9.desc: Rules of Izhar, Idgham, Iqlab, and Ikhfa.
qaida.step.10.title: Meem Sakin
qaida.step.10.desc: Three rules of Meem Sakin: Ikhfa Shafawi, Idgham Shafawi, and Izhar Shafawi.
qaida.step.11.title: Wajib Ghunnah
qaida.step.11.desc: Compulsory nasal resonance when Noon or Meem bears a Shaddah.
qaida.step.12.title: Madd Rules
qaida.step.12.desc: Elongation rules: Natural Madd (Asli) and Secondary Madd (Far'ee).
qaida.step.13.title: Rules of Lam
qaida.step.13.desc: Rules of Lam in the Name of Allah and Solar / Lunar Lam.
qaida.step.14.title: Ra & Lam Mastery
qaida.step.14.desc: Heavy (Tafkheem) and Light (Tarqeeq) pronunciation of Ra and Lam.
qaida.step.15.title: Muqattaat & Qalqalah
qaida.step.15.desc: Opening Quranic letters and the 5 bouncing echo letters (Qutb Jad).
qaida.step.16.title: Waqf Rules
qaida.step.16.desc: Stopping symbols and proper techniques for pausing during recitation.
qaida.step.17.title: Pure Tilawat
qaida.step.17.desc: Reciting complete Ayahs and short Surahs with full Tajweed mastery.
qaida.track.1.title: Letter Recognition
qaida.track.1.desc: Learn each of the 28 Arabic letters individually with correct makhraj.

qaida.track.2.desc: Learn how letters connect and change appearance in words.

basics.chapter.1.title: What is Iman?
basics.chapter.1.definition: Iman means believing in Allah and the truths He revealed with all your heart.
basics.chapter.1.story: Little Amin looked up at the stars and thought, "Who created such a beautiful creation?" Mother said, "Allah is the Creator of everything. We do not see Him, but we see His creations and trust Him." Amin learned that Iman is not just words; it shines through faith, good deeds, and trusting Allah.
basics.chapter.1.quiz.1.q: Where does Iman reside as belief?
basics.chapter.1.quiz.2.q: Who is the Creator of everything?
basics.chapter.1.quiz.3.q: How do we see signs of Allah without seeing Him?
basics.chapter.1.quiz.5.q: What is the relationship between good deeds and Iman?
basics.chapter.1.quiz.6.q: Why do we strive to speak the truth?
basics.chapter.1.quiz.7.q: From whom do we seek help in difficult times?
basics.chapter.1.quiz.8.q: What do we say when receiving a blessing?
basics.chapter.1.quiz.9.q: What do we do when we make a mistake?
basics.chapter.1.quiz.9.a: Seek forgiveness from Allah and correct it
basics.chapter.1.quiz.10.q: Is Iman complete with words alone?
basics.chapter.1.quiz.10.a: No, faith and good deeds are also essential
basics.chapter.2.title: What is Aqeedah?
basics.chapter.2.definition: Aqeedah is the foundation of Islamic belief—the fundamental truths that a Muslim accepts wholeheartedly.
basics.chapter.2.story: At school, the teacher spoke about the foundation of a building. When the foundation is strong, the house stands firm. Islamic faith is just like that—Allah is One, He is our Lord; His Messengers showed people the true path. To learn sound beliefs, Amin asks questions to his parents and trusted teachers.
basics.chapter.2.quiz.3.q: Who is our Creator and Sustainer?
basics.chapter.2.quiz.7.q: Remembering the Last Day makes us do what?
basics.chapter.2.quiz.8.q: Who to ask when having faith questions?
basics.chapter.2.quiz.9.q: Is anyone else a creator like Allah?
basics.chapter.2.quiz.10.q: What is the best way to learn sound Aqeedah?
basics.chapter.3.title: What is Islam?
basics.chapter.3.definition: Islam means worshipping Allah alone, obeying His commands, and treating people with kindness and excellence.
basics.chapter.3.story: Amin's friend asked, "Does Islam only mean praying?" Amin replied, "Prayer is very important; alongside it, speaking the truth, respecting parents, and being merciful are also teachings of Islam." They decided to do a good deed every day and learn the five daily prayers.
basics.chapter.3.quiz.2.q: What is the core teaching of Islam?
basics.chapter.3.quiz.2.a: Obedience to Allah and righteous living
basics.chapter.3.quiz.3.q: What kind of deed is prayer?
basics.chapter.3.quiz.6.a: No, we show kindness and respect
basics.chapter.3.quiz.7.q: For whose pleasure is worship done?
basics.chapter.3.quiz.8.q: Is Islam only a set of rituals?
basics.chapter.3.quiz.8.a: No, it is guidance for all of life
basics.chapter.3.quiz.9.q: What do we demonstrate by helping others?
basics.chapter.3.quiz.10.a: From Quran, Sunnah, and trusted teachers
basics.chapter.4.title: Halal and Haram
basics.chapter.4.definition: Halal means permissible in Islam; Haram means forbidden in Islam. When unsure, we ask knowledgeable elders rather than guessing.
basics.chapter.4.story: Seeing a new snack package at the shop, Amin wondered about its ingredients. Instead of deciding himself, he asked his father. His father checked the verified ingredients. Amin learned that whenever in doubt about deeds or food, we should verify through trusted guidance.
basics.chapter.4.quiz.3.q: Whom to ask when in doubt?
basics.chapter.4.quiz.4.q: Is it right to guess rulings by oneself?
basics.chapter.4.quiz.4.a: No, we learn and verify first
basics.chapter.4.quiz.5.q: What to do when misunderstanding something?
basics.chapter.4.quiz.6.q: From where do we learn Islamic rulings?
basics.chapter.4.quiz.7.q: What to do hearing unverified opinions?
basics.chapter.4.quiz.8.q: Is it okay to pressure friends to eat forbidden things?
basics.chapter.4.quiz.9.q: From whom to learn food rules?
basics.chapter.4.quiz.10.q: What is the goal of choosing Halal food?
basics.chapter.5.title: Clothing and Modesty
basics.chapter.5.definition: We wear clean, comfortable, and modest clothing that respects Islamic decency.
basics.chapter.5.story: Before going out to play, Amin put on clean and modest clothes. His mother smiled and said, "Modesty brings beauty to a believer." Amin felt proud to dress neatly and respectfully.
basics.chapter.5.quiz.1.q: What kind of clothing should a Muslim wear?
basics.chapter.5.quiz.2.q: What does modesty bring to a believer?
basics.chapter.5.quiz.3.q: Should we take care of cleanliness in clothing?
basics.chapter.5.quiz.5.q: What should we say when wearing new clothes?
basics.chapter.5.quiz.7.q: Should clothes be comfortable for prayer?
basics.chapter.5.quiz.8.q: Who sets the standards of modesty?
basics.chapter.5.quiz.9.q: How should we treat those with simple clothes?
basics.chapter.5.quiz.10.q: What is true inner beauty in Islam?
basics.chapter.6.title: Beautiful Speech
basics.chapter.6.definition: We speak the truth gently and respectfully. We avoid bad language, lies, insult, and backbiting.
basics.chapter.6.story: When someone spoke rudely in the playground, Amin did not retaliate with harsh words. He responded politely and walked away with dignity. His friends praised his calm demeanor and saw how good speech diffuses anger.
basics.chapter.6.quiz.4.q: What to do when feeling angry?
basics.chapter.6.quiz.4.a: Stay silent or seek refuge in Allah
basics.chapter.6.quiz.6.q: How to address parents and elders?
basics.chapter.6.quiz.7.q: What is a good word considered in Islam?
basics.chapter.6.quiz.8.q: What greeting do we offer when meeting people?
basics.chapter.6.quiz.9.q: What should we do if we accidentally hurt someone with words?
basics.chapter.7.title: Noble Character
basics.chapter.7.definition: Honesty, patience, cleanliness, mercy, and responsibility—these noble traits reflect Islam in our daily conduct.
basics.chapter.7.story: Amin saw an elderly neighbor carrying heavy grocery bags. He immediately ran up and politely offered to carry them to the door. The neighbor smiled and prayed for him. Amin felt immense joy in helping.
basics.chapter.7.quiz.1.q: What was the primary mission of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)?
basics.chapter.7.quiz.3.q: How do we treat our neighbors?
basics.chapter.7.quiz.5.q: What do we do when finding lost property?
basics.chapter.7.quiz.5.a: Try to return it to the owner
basics.chapter.7.quiz.6.q: Is showing mercy to animals rewarded?
basics.chapter.7.quiz.7.q: What is smiling at your brother considered?
basics.chapter.7.quiz.8.q: How should we act when receiving help?
basics.chapter.7.quiz.9.q: Does Islam encourage cleanliness of the environment?
basics.chapter.7.quiz.10.q: What is the heaviness of good character on the Day of Judgment?
basics.chapter.8.title: Treating People with Respect
basics.chapter.8.definition: We treat parents, relatives, teachers, neighbors, and friends with justice, kindness, and honor.
basics.chapter.8.story: Amin shared his pencils and coloring books with a classmate who had forgotten theirs. The teacher smiled and appreciated Amin's generosity and brotherly spirit.
basics.chapter.8.quiz.1.q: Who holds the greatest right to our good companionship?
basics.chapter.8.quiz.2.q: How should we treat our teachers?
basics.chapter.8.quiz.3.q: Is maintaining ties of kinship important?
basics.chapter.8.quiz.4.q: How to treat younger siblings or children?
basics.chapter.8.quiz.7.q: Is sharing food with friends encouraged?
basics.chapter.8.quiz.10.q: Who is the best of people in the Hadith?
basics.chapter.9.title: Halal Food
basics.chapter.9.definition: We choose wholesome, pure, and lawful food that Allah has made permissible for us.
basics.chapter.9.story: At lunchtime, Amin washed his hands, sat down nicely, said "Bismillah", and ate with his right hand. He chewed quietly and thanked Allah after finishing with "Alhamdulillah".
basics.chapter.9.quiz.1.q: What do we say before eating?
basics.chapter.9.quiz.2.q: Which hand do we eat with?
basics.chapter.9.quiz.3.q: What do we say after eating?
basics.chapter.9.quiz.4.q: Should we wash hands before eating?
basics.chapter.9.quiz.6.q: Should we criticize food we dislike?
basics.chapter.9.quiz.6.a: No, leave it respectfully if not eating
basics.chapter.9.quiz.7.q: How should water be drank according to Sunnah?
basics.chapter.9.quiz.7.a: Sitting down and in three sips
basics.chapter.9.quiz.10.q: Does wholesome food affect prayer and heart?
basics.chapter.10.title: Avoiding Haram Food
basics.chapter.10.definition: Islam forbids certain foods and drinks for our spiritual and physical well-being. We verify ingredients when uncertain.
basics.chapter.10.story: At a store abroad, Amin noticed an attractive candy with suspicious gelatin. Remembering his lesson, he checked with his father. They found it contained pork derivatives and chose a delicious Halal alternative instead.
basics.chapter.10.quiz.3.q: What if we eat something Haram unknowingly?
basics.chapter.10.quiz.3.a: Seek Allah's forgiveness, no sin if unaware
basics.chapter.10.quiz.4.q: What should we do when ingredients are doubtful?
basics.chapter.10.quiz.5.q: Can we offer Haram food to others?
basics.chapter.10.quiz.6.q: Why did Allah prohibit certain foods?
basics.chapter.10.quiz.6.a: For our physical and spiritual harm prevention
basics.chapter.10.quiz.7.q: Is Halal food always clean and wholesome?
basics.chapter.10.quiz.9.q: Who teaches us the dietary laws?
basics.chapter.10.quiz.9.a: Allah and His Prophet (peace be upon him)
basics.chapter.10.quiz.10.q: What is our attitude towards Allah's prohibitions?
basics.chapter.10.quiz.10.a: We hear and we obey with joy
seerah.story.abu_umair.body: Anas (RA)'s younger brother Abu Umair had a small pet bird. When the Prophet visited their home, he would lovingly ask the boy about his little bird. He paid careful attention even to the small joys of children.
seerah.story.abu_umair.lesson: To build a warm bond with someone, listen carefully to what brings them joy.
seerah.story.hasan_kindness.title: Affection for Hasan (RA)
seerah.story.hasan_kindness.subtitle: Showing mercy is a noble habit
seerah.story.hasan_kindness.body: One day the Prophet kissed his grandson Hasan (RA). A bystander remarked that he had never kissed any of his own children. The Prophet explained: He who does not show mercy will not be shown mercy.
seerah.story.hasan_kindness.lesson: Always treat both young and old with tenderness and mercy.
seerah.story.first_revelation.title: The First Revelation in Cave Hira
seerah.story.first_revelation.subtitle: A new beginning of knowledge and truth
seerah.story.first_revelation.body: Before prophethood, Muhammad spent quiet contemplative time in Cave Hira. There, the first revelation came to him. Khadijah (RA) comforted him with courage and stood firmly by his side. Thus began the transmission of the Quranic message.
seerah.story.first_revelation.lesson: Give strength to family in difficult times and stand with the truth.
seerah.story.zamzam_baby.title: The Story of Zamzam Water
seerah.story.zamzam_baby.subtitle: The reward of trusting in Allah
seerah.story.zamzam_baby.body: Hajar (RA) found herself alone in the desert of Makkah with her infant Ismail. As the water ran out, she ran between the hills of Safa and Marwah searching for water. By Allah's decree, the well of Zamzam sprang from beneath the child's feet.
seerah.story.zamzam_baby.lesson: Trust in Allah even in the greatest hardships; He never abandons us.
seerah.story.kaaba_corner.title: Arbitration at the Rebuilding of the Kaaba
seerah.story.kaaba_corner.subtitle: Resolving tribal disputes with wisdom
seerah.story.kaaba_corner.body: When rebuilding the Kaaba, the tribes argued over who would place the Black Stone. The young Muhammad placed the stone on a cloak and had every tribal leader hold an edge, resolving the conflict peacefully.
seerah.story.kaaba_corner.lesson: Resolve disagreements with wisdom, justice, and collective participation.
seerah.story.khadija_trust.title: Khadijah (RA)'s Steadfast Faith
seerah.story.khadija_trust.subtitle: Support and trust in times of distress
seerah.story.khadija_trust.body: When the Prophet received revelation and feared for himself, Khadijah reassured him: 'By Allah, Allah will never disgrace you, for you maintain ties of kinship, help the poor, and support the truth.'
seerah.story.khadija_trust.lesson: Good character and service to humanity earn divine protection and human trust.
seerah.story.bilal_patience.title: The Patience of Bilal (RA)
seerah.story.bilal_patience.subtitle: Steadfastness upon faith under persecution
seerah.story.bilal_patience.body: Under the scorching desert heat, heavy rocks were placed on Bilal's chest to force him to renounce Islam. Yet his heart remained firm and his tongue repeated: 'Ahad, Ahad' (Allah is One).
seerah.story.bilal_patience.lesson: True faith cannot be broken by worldly pressure or hardship.
seerah.story.anas_servant.title: Ten Years in the Prophet's Care
seerah.story.anas_servant.subtitle: Gentleness and compassion toward assistants
seerah.story.anas_servant.body: Anas (RA) served the Prophet for ten years. He said: 'He never once said 'Uff' to me, nor did he ask why I did something or why I failed to do something.'
seerah.story.anas_servant.lesson: Treat domestic workers, assistants, and younger ones with immense gentleness.
seerah.story.migration_madina.title: The Hijrah to Madinah
seerah.story.migration_madina.subtitle: Trust in Allah and strategic planning
seerah.story.migration_madina.body: When the Quraysh plotted against the Prophet, he migrated to Madinah with Abu Bakr (RA). Taking refuge in Cave Thawr, Abu Bakr worried, but the Prophet said: 'Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us.'
seerah.story.migration_madina.lesson: Combine careful effort with complete reliance on Allah.
seerah.story.badr_dua.title: The Supplication at Badr
seerah.story.badr_dua.subtitle: Turning to Allah with humility before the trial
seerah.story.badr_dua.body: On the eve of the Battle of Badr, the Prophet spent the night in tearful supplication, raising his hands so high his cloak fell. Allah answered and granted victory to the believers.
seerah.story.badr_dua.lesson: Supplication is the believer's greatest weapon in any difficulty.
seerah.story.conquest_mercy.title: Mercy at the Conquest of Makkah
seerah.story.conquest_mercy.subtitle: Forgiving those who persecuted you
seerah.story.conquest_mercy.body: When the Prophet entered Makkah victorious, the people who had driven him out and hurt him stood before him. Instead of revenge, he announced: 'Go, for you are free.'
seerah.story.conquest_mercy.lesson: The greatest victory lies in forgiveness, humility, and mercy.
seerah.story.taif_patience.title: Patience and Forgiveness at Taif
seerah.story.taif_patience.subtitle: Praying for guidance for those who hurt you
seerah.story.taif_patience.body: When the people of Taif stoned the Prophet and injured him, the angel of mountains offered to crush the town. The Prophet replied: 'No, I hope Allah brings from their descendants people who will worship Him alone.'
seerah.story.taif_patience.lesson: Wish guidance and good even for those who wrong you.
seerah.story.suleiman_wisdom.title: Wisdom of the Ant
seerah.story.suleiman_wisdom.subtitle: Caring for all living creatures
seerah.story.suleiman_wisdom.body: Prophet Sulaiman (AS) heard an ant warning her colony to seek shelter so the army wouldn't crush them unknowingly. Sulaiman smiled and praised Allah for granting him the wisdom to understand.
seerah.story.suleiman_wisdom.lesson: Every tiny creature has value; always walk the earth with mindfulness.
seerah.story.madinah_brotherhood.title: The Brotherhood of Madinah
seerah.story.madinah_brotherhood.subtitl: Selfless sharing between Muhajirun and Ansar
seerah.story.madinah_brotherhood.body: In Madinah, the Prophet paired each immigrant from Makkah with a local helper from Madinah. The Ansar shared their homes, wealth, and farms selflessly with their new brothers.
seerah.story.madinah_brotherhood.lesson: Share generously with others and build genuine community brotherhood.
seerah.story.uhud_wound.title: Steadfastness at Uhud
seerah.story.uhud_wound.subtitle: Remaining steadfast when plans face adversity
seerah.story.uhud_wound.body: When the Prophet was wounded at Uhud and blood flowed on his face, he wiped the blood and prayed: 'O Allah, forgive my people, for they do not know.'
seerah.story.uhud_wound.lesson: Meet adversity with prayer and patience rather than resentment.
seerah.story.marriage_khadija.title: Trust in Character: Khadijah (RA)
seerah.story.marriage_khadija.subtitle: Honesty in trade and life shines bright
seerah.story.marriage_khadija.body: Khadijah entrusted Muhammad with her trade caravan because of his honesty (Al-Amin). Impressed by his integrity, trustworthiness, and noble manners, she chose him as her lifelong companion.
seerah.story.marriage_khadija.lesson: Honesty and integrity in work earn lasting respect and trust.
seerah.story.isra_miraj.title: The Night Journey (Isra and Mi'raj)
seerah.story.isra_miraj.subtitle: The gift of five daily prayers
seerah.story.isra_miraj.body: In a single night, the Prophet was taken from Makkah to Jerusalem, and then ascended through the heavens where Allah gifted the Muslim community the five daily prayers.
seerah.story.isra_miraj.lesson: Daily prayer is our direct conversation and spiritual ascension to Allah.
seerah.story.arqam_house.title: The House of Al-Arqam
seerah.story.arqam_house.subtitle: Learning and growing in small circles
seerah.story.arqam_house.body: In the early days of Islam, believers met secretly at the house of young Al-Arqam to study the Quran, pray together, and support one another in faith.
seerah.story.arqam_house.lesson: Dedicate time to learning in peaceful and supportive environments.
seerah.story.farewell_sermon.title: The Farewell Sermon
seerah.story.farewell_sermon.subtitle: Universal equality and human dignity
seerah.story.farewell_sermon.body: At Mount Arafat, the Prophet declared: 'All mankind is from Adam and Eve. An Arab has no superiority over a non-Arab, nor a white person over a black person, except by piety.'
seerah.story.farewell_sermon.lesson: All human beings are equal; honor and nobility come only through righteous deeds.
seerah.story.hadith_smile.title: Smiling is Charity
seerah.story.hadith_smile.subtitle: Spreading joy and light around you
seerah.story.hadith_smile.body: Jarir (RA) said: 'The Prophet never looked at me except with a warm smile on his blessed face.' A sincere smile warms hearts and is recorded as charity.
seerah.story.hadith_smile.lesson: Greet everyone with warmth and a cheerful countenance.
seerah.story.food_sharing.title: Sharing the Blessing of Food
seerah.story.food_sharing.subtitle: Food for two is sufficient for three
seerah.story.food_sharing.body: The Prophet taught: 'The food of two people is sufficient for three, and the food of three is sufficient for four.' Eating together brings barakah (divine blessing).
seerah.story.food_sharing.lesson: Share food and hospitality willingly; it multiplies blessings.
seerah.story.muadh_kindness.title: Advice to Mu'adh (RA)
seerah.story.muadh_kindness.subtitle: Teaching gently and making matters easy
seerah.story.muadh_kindness.body: Sending Mu'adh to Yemen, the Prophet advised him: 'Make things easy and do not make them difficult; give glad tidings and do not repel people.'
seerah.story.muadh_kindness.lesson: Approach education and religion with gentleness, patience, and facilitation.
seerah.story.ashab_suffa.title: The Companions of the Bench (Suffah)
seerah.story.ashab_suffa.subtitle: Dedication to sacred knowledge and simplicity
seerah.story.ashab_suffa.body: At the rear of the Prophet's Mosque lived students of knowledge who dedicated their lives to learning the Quran and Sunnah in noble simplicity. The Prophet cared for them as a father.
seerah.story.ashab_suffa.lesson: Honoring knowledge and supporting students is a virtuous path.
